title: The RCW 38 cluster in infrared light
caption: The star cluster RCW 38 in infrared light, imaged by the VISTA telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Gas, dust and stars mix into a rich, tangled landscape in this 80-million-pixel picture of the star cluster RCW 38, in the constellation Vela. The cluster is young, holds about 2000 stars and is full of star-forming activity.

The image was taken with ESO's Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for Astronomy (VISTA) in Chile's Atacama Desert. VISTA observes in infrared light, which can pass through most of the dust in this region. In visible light, that dust would block much of the view.

Looking behind the dust, VISTA reveals young stars still wrapped in dusty cocoons. It also shows cold objects called brown dwarfs, sometimes described as failed stars because they never became massive enough to shine like true stars. Together they show what goes on inside a young stellar nursery.
scale: RCW 38 is about 5500 light-years away, according to ESO.

understand.summary: This image comes from the VIRCAM camera on ESO's VISTA telescope, in near-infrared light through J (1.25 μm), H (1.65 μm) and Ks (2.15 μm) filters. The colors assigned to each filter are not published.
